Black Friday might technically be over, but all the best gaming PC deals we've seen are still very much live. Right now, with AI driving up component prices, buying a gaming PC is one of the easiest ways to offset the very worst price hikes on SSDs, RAM, and GPUs, with buying a pre-built PC often cheaper than DIY in late 2026.

A quick look at part prices will tell you this. The RTX 5080 GPU now costs around $2,000, while the RTX 5090 has all but disappeared from the consumer market. 32GB of DDR5-6000 RAM now costs $500, while a 1TB SSD is $250. Black Friday has given us some deals on these prices, but buying a gaming PC is still more economical in many cases.

We're tracking the best configurations and rigs at Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy, and Walmart, as well as offerings from vendors like HP, MSI, Dell, and more. We use our hands-on testing experience, extensive benchmark data, and price tracking to find you real deals.

November 28, 2026 – 2:36 AM Welcome to Saturday and our ongoing coverage of the best gaming PC deals on Black Friday. While some of our top deals have expired, many more remain available, and we expect new offerings to emerge over the weekend.

November 28, 2026 – 2:39 AM The biggest draw to buying a pre-built gaming PC in 2026, aside from the usual benefits of convenience and dealing with just one vendor for shipping and warranties, etc., is price. Most Nvidia RTX GPUs are between 60-200% more expensive than their MSRP. Likewise, RAM and SSD prices are through the roof, making building your own rig a daunting task. The team is here to help you find pre-built alternatives.
